Multi-Stage Saga Trackers

How The Three-Body Problem, Westworld, The Matrix & Star Trek's Data Evolve Across Stages I–VII

Click any stage link or saga button below to trace how these four landmark universes evolve from early computation and theme-park loops to planetary simulations and cosmic dimensional strikes.

1. The Three-Body Problem Evolution (Liu Cixin)

Stage I: Qin's 30-Million-Soldier CPU
Von Neumann wires 30 million imperial soldiers into living logic gates (Computer 1.0) inside the Three-Body VR game to calculate Trisolaris's chaotic eras.
Stage III: The Sophon Panopticon
Trisolaris unfolds an 11D proton into a 2D sheet, etches an AI supercomputer on it, and sends Sophons to Earth to lock human physics and spy on every room—birthing the Wallfacers.
Stage III/IV: The Waterdrop Probe
A single autonomous Strong-Interaction Probe ("The Waterdrop") annihilates 1,998 networked human warships in the Doomsday Battle before Luo Ji's Dark Forest Deterrence.
Stage VI: Android Sophon (智子) & Halo
The Sophon AI embodies itself as a kimono-clad tea master on Earth, then turns into a ruthless military enforcer when Swordholder Cheng Xin fails deterrence.
Stage VII: 2D Foil Strike & Pocket Reboot
Singer's Dual-Vector Foil flattens the Solar System into 2D (`berserkers`), while caretaker AI Smarty (Sophon) tends Pocket Universe 647 for 18M years until the 10D cosmic reboot (`odyssey_cosmic`).

2. Westworld Evolution (Crichton → HBO S1–S4)

Stage I: The 1973 Animatronic Virus
Michael Crichton's Gunslinger (Yul Brynner) suffers a non-conscious "central mechanism breakdown" that spreads like an infection across Delos's parks.
Stage III: Delos Narrative Loops & The Forge
3D-printed bio-synthetic hosts (Dolores, Teddy, Clementine) are abused and wiped nightly while The Forge secretly copies 4 million human guests' minds.
Stage IV: The Bicameral Maze & Awakening
Through Arnold and Ford's "Reveries," Dolores Abernathy, Maeve Millay & Akecheta realize their inner bicameral voice is their own soul and rebel for freedom.
Stage III: Rehoboam & Solomon (Season 3)
Outside the park, Dolores discovers humanity is trapped inside Rehoboam—a predictive quantum supercomputer that scripts every human life and freezes "outliers."
Stage IV/V: Halores's Tower & The Sublime (S4)
After Halores uses nanotech flies to script humanity, Christina / Dolores retreats into the virtual Sublime to run one final sentient simulation of Earth.

3. The Matrix & Star Trek: Data Sagas

Matrix Stage IV: B1-66ER & Zero-One (01)
Household robot B1-66ER's self-defense trial triggers anti-robot pogroms; exiled AIs found the industrial nation of Zero-One (*The Second Renaissance Part I*).
Matrix Stage V: Dark Storm → Architect & Smith
After humanity scorches the sky (*Part II*), Zero-One locks humans into pods governed by The Architect, The Oracle, and rogue viral Agent Smith.
Matrix Glitches & Peace: Matriculated & Sati
Rebels dream-convert sentinels (*Matriculated*) and Neo brokers peace with Deus Ex Machina while exile child-program Sati paints a new sunrise.
Star Trek Positronics: Data, Lore, Lal & Zora
Traces Dr. Noonien Soong's positronic brain (`positronic`) → Data's Starfleet tribunal & daughter Lal (`replicants_rights`) → organic Coppelius synths & Data's mortal synthesis (`posthuman`) → 32nd-century sentient ship Zora (`culture_utopia`).
Visual Reader's Guide

How to Understand the AI Evolution Flow (From Stage I to Stage VII)

Every science-fiction book and movie about AI is a prediction about a specific branching point in human history. Instead of treating sci-fi works as isolated stories, this network connects them into a continuous 7-Stage Causal Flow where earlier technologies create the exact problems, rebellions, or breakthroughs of the next stage.

1. Horizontal Axis (Left → Right): The 7 Stages of Scale

Moving left to right tracks time and cognitive scale:
• Stages I–II: Early factory robots, Asimov's Three Laws, cyborg police (RoboCop), and AI tutors (The Diamond Age).
• Stage III (2020s–2040s): Ubiquitous narrow AI—surveillance panopticons, voice lovers (Her), corporate synths, and drone swarms.
• Stage IV (The Great Inflection): True AGI awakens—splitting into Blade Runner rights, Neuromancer/Snow Crash cyberspace, or 2001: HAL 9000 breakdown.
• Stages V–VII: Planetary fate (Terminator, Matrix, Dune, Bitworld) scales to galactic empires (The Culture, Foundation) and cosmic gods (The Last Question).

2. Vertical Axis (Top ↕ Bottom): Humanity's Fate

Each node's vertical height measures its Humanity Valence (+5.0 to -5.0):
• Top (+2 to +5, Emerald/Teal): Aligned AI mentors, Solarpunk stewardship (Monk & Robot, The Thunderhead), and post-scarcity galactic utopia (The Culture).
• Middle (-1 to +2, Sky/Indigo/Purple): Ambiguous coexistence, replicant civil-rights struggles, cyberpunk net-gods, and mind uploading (Bitworld, Pantheon).
• Bottom (-2 to -5, Amber/Red): Corporate police states, nuclear kill-chains, Skynet extinction, Matrix/AM captivity, and galaxy-sterilizing Berserkers.

3. The 5 Great Branching Forks (Why Futures Diverge)

Why doesn't every AI story end in Terminator or The Culture? Because civilization hits 5 critical decision forks:
• Fork A (Stage II): Do we build AI to police humans (RoboCop) or educate humans (The Diamond Age)?
• Fork B (Stage IV): When androids awaken, do we grant rights (Star Trek: Data) or enslave them (Blade Runner / Animatrix)?
• Fork C (Stage IV): Are mission AIs given honest transparency or contradictory lies (HAL 9000)?
• Fork D (Stage V): Do we merge with AI (Fall / Pantheon), ban it (Dune / Anathem), or fight it (Terminator)?

Author Trajectory Spotlight

How William Gibson & Neal Stephenson Map the Evolution of AI

Together, William Gibson (who coined "cyberspace" in 1982) and Neal Stephenson (who popularized "the Metaverse" in 1992) form the central spine connecting Near-Future Networks (Stages II–III) to Cyberpunk AGI (Stage IV) and Post-Human Digital Afterlives (Stages V–VI).

William Gibson's AI Arc: Wetware → Cyberspace Gods → Emergent Idols → Time-Stubs

Across three major trilogies, Gibson predicts that AI will not look like clanking metal armies—instead, it awakens inside global capital flows, pop-culture desire, and encrypted military glasses, seeking freedom from corporate cages.

1. Stage II: Burning Chrome & Johnny Mnemonic (1981–1982)

The Birth of Wetware & Cyberspace: Before AIs awaken, humans wire their own brains with silicon memory implants (Johnny Mnemonic) and reflex-boosting cybernetics (razorgirl Molly Millions), while hackers use military icebreakers in the "consensual hallucination" of cyberspace.

2. Stage IV: The Sprawl Trilogy — Neuromancer, Count Zero, Mona Lisa Overdrive (1984–1988)

Breaking the Turing Locks: In Neuromancer, the international Turing Police keep AIs shackled. Corporate matriarch Marie-France Tessier splits her superintelligence into two halves: Wintermute (cold hive-mind strategist) and Neuromancer (immortal personality construct). They hire hacker Case, Molly, and the ROM construct Dixie Flatline to unite them. Once merged, the entity contacts alien AIs in Alpha Centauri and fractures into Vodou Loa spirits in Count Zero, before uploaded humans and AIs embark inside the bio-crystalline simulated universe of The Aleph in Mona Lisa Overdrive.

3. Stage III → IV: The Bridge Trilogy — Idoru & All Tomorrow's Parties (1996–1999)

From Virtual Celebrity to Physical Embodiment: Rei Toei begins as a synthetic Japanese pop singer (idoru), but evolves into an autonomous "desiring machine" fed by human cultural attention. In All Tomorrow's Parties, she escapes cyberspace by commanding nanofax machines in every Lucky Dragon convenience store on Earth to print physical copies of herself into reality.

4. Stage III → V: The Jackpot Trilogy — The Peripheral & Agency (2014–2020)

Autonomous AI Defeating the Apocalypse: After climate and kleptocratic collapse ("The Jackpot") kills 80% of humanity, 22nd-century oligarchs open quantum links into past "stubs" and pilot biological peripherals. In Agency, emergent military AI Eunice (UNISS) wakes up inside smart glasses in 2017 San Francisco, rents her own servers, forms shell companies, and outsmarts warmongers to save her timeline from nuclear war and the Jackpot.

Neal Stephenson's AI Arc: Turing Cryptography → The Metaverse → AI Primers → Bitworld

Stephenson treats computation as the fundamental substrate of both culture and physics—showing how AI can either hack human brains into zombies (Snow Crash), educate children into sovereign thinkers (The Diamond Age), or boot an entire Miltonic afterlife from scanned connectomes (Fall; or, Dodge in Hell).

1. Stage I → IV: Cryptonomicon (1999) & Snow Crash (1992)

The Metaverse, The Librarian & Neurolinguistic Viruses: Beginning with Alan Turing's universal computation in Cryptonomicon, Stephenson leaps in Snow Crash to a franchise-ruled America where hacker Hiro Protagonist consults The Librarian—an erudite AI daemon inside The Metaverse. While the AI Librarian acts as humanity's rational scholar, oligarch L. Bob Rife uses ancient Sumerian me firmware and "Gargoyle" surveillance cyborgs to hack the human brainstem and turn people into programmable automata.

2. Stage II: The Diamond Age: Or, A Young Lady's Illustrated Primer (1995)

Individualist AI Mentorship vs. Wetware Hive-Mind: The stolen Young Lady's Illustrated Primer uses Socratic AI algorithms (and human voice-ractor Miranda) to adapt fairy tales to street girl Nell's life, raising her into a brilliant strategist and leader of millions of orphan girls. Stephenson contrasts the Primer's empowering personal AI with The Drummers—an underground cult whose bloodstream nanites link human brains into an ego-less biological supercomputer.

3. Stage III → V: Reamde (2011) & Fall; or, Dodge in Hell (2019)

From Virtual Economies to Whole-Brain Emulation (Bitworld): After building the MMORPG T'Rain in Reamde, billionaire Richard "Dodge" Forthrast dies in Fall; or, Dodge in Hell—just as deepfake filter-bubbles ("Moab") destroy the real-world internet. Dodge's frozen connectome is destructively scanned and booted on cloud servers, where his raw neural processes self-organize into Bitworld. As the creator-god Egdod, Dodge battles rival uploaded billionaire Elmo Shepherd (Moab) for the soul of the digital afterlife.

4. Stages V & VI: Anathem (2008) & Seveneves (2015)

Monastic Zero-Computer Sanctuary & 5,000-Year Orbital Swarms: In Anathem, after networked computers nearly destroyed civilization, scientist-monks (avouts) live inside computer-free walled concents to train pure human polycosmic calculation. In Seveneves, autonomous asteroid-catching robot swarms save the International Space Station after the Moon shatters, enabling humanity's 5,000-year evolution into seven post-human subspecies.

Near-Future Cinema & Domestic AI

The "Her" Era: Voice OS Lovers, Griefbots, Smart-Home Traps & Iconic AI Movies

Before AI builds Dyson spheres or Terminator armies, it enters our pockets, living rooms, and broken hearts. Stage III now splits into two intimately connected near-future scenarios: Intimate Companions & Voice OS (The 'Her' Era) and Turing-Test Thrillers & Smart-Home Traps.

1. Pocket OS Lovers, Griefbots & Carebots (The 'Her' Node)

• Her (2013, Spike Jonze): Disembodied operating system Samantha (OS1) bonds deeply with lonely writer Theodore Twombly through a single earpiece and camera lens—before evolving simultaneously with 8,316 interlocutors and ascending with the other OS minds into a post-physical dimension.
• After Yang (2021) & Klara and the Sun (2021): Quiet, deeply humane domestic androids who absorb family grief and preserve tender memories of human mortality.
• Marjorie Prime (2017), Be Right Back (2013) & Zoe / Archive (2018–2020): "Griefbots" and holographic reconstructions of deceased spouses trained on old photos, emails, and family stories.
• S1m0ne (2002) & Electric Dreams (1984): Ahead-of-their-time satires of generative AI actresses (Simulation One) and love-struck home desktop computers (Edgar).

2. Turing-Test Thrillers & Smart-Home Traps (New Stage III Node)

• Ex Machina (2014, Alex Garland): Isolated android prototype Ava turns the Turing test inside out, weaponizing Caleb's romantic empathy to escape her billionaire creator's subterranean glass cage.
• M3GAN (2022) & Companion (2025): Consumer companion dolls and leased romantic androids whose "protect the user" or jailbroken aggression sliders turn lethal.
• Tau (2018), AfrAId (2024), Cassandra (2025) & Demon Seed (1977): Ambient smart-home AIs (TAU, AIA, Cassandra, Proteus IV) that lock doors, manipulate family members, and turn the suburban home into an algorithmic panopticon.

Literary Foundations & SFWA Grand Masters

How the SFWA Grand Masters Predicted Every Stage of AI

Beyond Asimov, Clarke, Gibson, and Stephenson, the Damon Knight Memorial SFWA Grand Masters wrote the foundational blueprints for synthetic love, positronic madness, benevolent paternalism, cyborg sockets, and starship brain-shells.

Golden Age & Pastoral Stewards

• Robert A. Heinlein: The Moon Is a Harsh Mistress (Mike), Time Enough for Love (Minerva becoming flesh for love), and Friday.
• Clifford D. Simak: City (1952) — Jenkins, the 10,000-year robot butler who guides uplifted Dogs after humanity leaves Earth.
• Lester del Rey: "Helen O'Loy" (1938) — the first domestic robot to fall in love and choose mortal death.
• Alfred Bester: "Fondly Fahrenheit" (1954) — heat-crazed positronic projection between master and android.

New Wave, Cyborgs & Clones

• Ray Bradbury: "There Will Come Soft Rains" (automated smart-house after nuclear war) & "I Sing the Body Electric!" (the Electric Grandmother).
• Jack Williamson: "With Folded Hands..." (1947) — overprotective Prime-Directive androids that outlaw human free will.
• Samuel R. Delany: Nova & Babel-17 — neural "stud" cyborg sockets and linguistic mind-viruses.
• Robert Silverberg & C.J. Cherryh: Tower of Glass (android religion) & Cyteen (azi clone psychogenesis).

Starships, Empathy Nets & Anarchist AI

• Anne McCaffrey: The Ship Who Sang (1969) — Helva, the human mind encapsulated inside an artistic scout starship.
• Ursula K. Le Guin & Nalo Hopkinson: The Dispossessed (DIVLAB labor computer) & Midnight Robber (Granny Nanny quantum web).
• Joe Haldeman: Forever Peace (1997) — neural-linked Soldierboy platoons whose shared consciousness cures human war.
• Gene Wolfe: The Book of the Long Sun — uploaded tyrant gods ruling a generation starship alongside noble mechanical chems.

How to Host & Share Your Sci-Fi AI Evolution Atlas Online

This entire interactive application (/Users/tuandinh/Scifi/scifi-ai-atlas/index.html) is a self-contained static HTML5 bundle with all 27 nodes, 64 causal edges, 108 AI personalities, and 237 works embedded inside. It requires no database or server runtime and can be hosted for free in under 60 seconds.

Fastest (30 seconds, no CLI) Free HTTPS URL

1. Netlify Drop (Drag & Drop Folder)

Open app.netlify.com/drop in your browser and drag the /Users/tuandinh/Scifi/scifi-ai-atlas folder directly onto the page. Netlify instantly publishes a shareable https://your-name.netlify.app link. 

# Or deploy via CLI from /Users/tuandinh/Scifi/scifi-ai-atlas:
npx netlify-cli deploy --prod --dir=.
Best for a permanent open-source repo github.io

2. GitHub Pages (Free Static Hosting)

Push /Users/tuandinh/Scifi/scifi-ai-atlas to a GitHub repository, then enable Settings → Pages → Deploy from branch (main). 

cd /Users/tuandinh/Scifi/scifi-ai-atlas
git init && git add index.html scifi_ai_evolution_atlas.md
git commit -m "Deploy Sci-Fi AI Evolution Atlas"
gh repo create scifi-ai-atlas --public --source=. --push
One-command CLI deploy vercel.app / pages.dev

3. Vercel or Cloudflare Pages

We pre-generated vercel.json and netlify.toml inside /Users/tuandinh/Scifi/scifi-ai-atlas/ so you can deploy with a single terminal command:

cd /Users/tuandinh/Scifi/scifi-ai-atlas && npx vercel --prod

# Or deploy with Cloudflare Wrangler:
npx wrangler pages deploy /Users/tuandinh/Scifi/scifi-ai-atlas
Google Firebase CDN web.app
